html:
SMTO-EXE-0001 — An earlier job is still holding what this step needs

GUID: 58c5ee27-44b8-4f4d-a8c0-b2a26f1d8b7e
Slug: resource-reconciliation-required
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO didn't run this step because an earlier job is still using the same thing, or stopped without SMTO knowing what it finished. Your new step hasn't started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look in the task for the Job recovery card. If the earlier job might still be working, select Wait until the job state changes. SMTO then continues by itself as soon as the earlier job lets go.
  2. If the earlier task shows as interrupted, open it and select Continue task. This lets SMTO check what the interrupted task already did before anything new runs.
  3. Only if you are sure the earlier job is stuck and its work no longer matters, select Resolve forcefully by terminating job, if it is available. This stops the earlier job for good, so use it only when you don't need its result.
  4. If none of these appear, select Copy error details in this panel. The details list which earlier jobs and items are blocking this step.

What success looks like

  • The Job recovery card disappears and the task continues with the new step.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before sending this request again. Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep sending the same request while the earlier job is unresolved; it will be blocked again and could get in that job's way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Execution was blocked because a conflicting job still owns the resource, an earlier job has unresolved effects, or an interrupted predecessor task has not been reconciled; the new operation was not executed.

What this means

  • Admission or continuation found conflicting owned work, unresolved historical effects or an interrupted predecessor that still needs reconciliation. Some producers also block after a long wait for an active owner. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Admission or continuation found conflicting owned work, unresolved historical effects or an interrupted predecessor that still needs reconciliation. Some producers also block after a long wait for an active owner.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the blocking job or predecessor, liveness, effect certainty and resource overlap; distinguish an active owner from ended work with uncertain effects.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the blocking job IDs and resource scope in the receipt or the task's Job recovery card. Let the owner finish (Wait until the job state changes), use Continue task on an interrupted predecessor so its effects are reconciled, or, only when the blocker is confirmed abandoned and the action is enabled, use Resolve forcefully by terminating job. Proceed only once resource admission permits the new operation.
  • Inspect the recorded blocker and reconcile it through its owning controls. Continue only after current resource admission permits the new operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The owning control flow settles the blocker and current admission permits this specific new operation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
